title: Rabbit Face Emoji 🐰 Meaning: Bunny, Easter and Beyond
description: The 🐰 rabbit face emoji means bunnies, Easter and soft, cute affection. Find out how it is used as a pet name, in fandoms, at Lunar New Year and in flirting.
summary: The 🐰 rabbit face emoji means a bunny, and with it sweetness, shyness and springtime. It peaks around Easter, marks the Year of the Rabbit in the Chinese zodiac, and doubles as a pet name for someone the sender finds adorable. In some contexts it hints at the Playboy bunny.
meaning: Nobody types “rabbit” when they send 🐰; they mean “bunny.” The emoji is a white or gray face with long upright ears and prominent front teeth, and it is used for pet rabbits, for anything small and soft, and above all for Easter. In the weeks before the holiday it appears on egg-hunt invitations, chocolate photos and school newsletters, then drops back to a steady trickle of pet and nickname use.

As a term of endearment, “bunny” is common between couples and from parents to small children, and the emoji carries that directly. Calling someone 🐰 says they are gentle, a bit timid or simply cute. It also describes behavior: a person who startles easily, eats a lot of salad or bounces with energy may get tagged with it. In K-pop fandoms, fans attach it to idols nicknamed for their rabbit-like smiles, most famously BTS’s Jungkook.

The rabbit has an adult side as well. The Playboy logo is a rabbit head, and “bunny” has meant a costumed hostess or, more loosely, a sexually confident woman for decades. The emoji occasionally nods to that, and to the old joke about rabbits breeding quickly. Fans of the Puerto Rican artist Bad Bunny use it as shorthand for him, which has nothing to do with either meaning.

contexts.label: On holidays
contexts.body: Easter is this emoji’s season. It stands for the Easter Bunny in messages to kids, on brunch plans and beside 🥚 and 🐣 in spring greetings. In East Asian communities and among anyone following the lunar zodiac, it marks the Year of the Rabbit and birthdays that fall in it, typically with red-envelope and lantern emojis.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: When someone you are dating sends 🐰, they are usually using it as a pet name or telling you that you look cute. It sits at the innocent end of flirting. A more suggestive reading is possible if the conversation is already heading that way, since “bunny” has a long association with pin-up imagery, but that is the exception.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Rabbit owners and rescue pages use it as their tag, and soft-aesthetic accounts scatter it among bows, ribbons and pastel hearts. Fandom comment sections are full of it: it is a recognized stand-in for Jungkook among BTS fans and for Bad Bunny among his listeners, so the same emoji means very different things under different posts.

examples.meaning: An Easter invitation; the emoji stands for the Easter Bunny.
An affectionate sign-off using “bunny” as a pet name.
A fan announcing concert tickets for Bad Bunny.

examples.text: She jumped a foot when the toaster popped 🐰
examples.meaning: Teases someone for being skittish, like a startled rabbit.
A Lunar New Year greeting for the rabbit zodiac year.

examples.text: All I’ve eaten today is carrots and lettuce 🐰
examples.meaning: A self-deprecating joke about eating “rabbit food.”

combos.meaning: Easter, egg hunts and holiday treats.
A pet rabbit’s snack, or a joke about healthy eating.
Common among BTS fans expressing love for Jungkook.
A soft, girly aesthetic used in captions and usernames.

confusedWith.difference: 🐇 is a full-body rabbit, usually shown mid-hop in profile. People pick it for speed, “down the rabbit hole” references and literal wildlife. 🐰 is the cuter face-only version preferred for Easter, pet names and fandom use.
🐭 has round ears and a pointed snout, and is tied to mice, cheese and Mickey Mouse. At small sizes the gray-and-pink coloring looks similar, but the tall ears on 🐰 are the giveaway.
🐹 is a chubby-cheeked orange-and-white rodent used for pocket pets and stuffed-cheek eating jokes. It shares the “small and cute” meaning but has no link to Easter or to the bunny nickname.

avoid: Avoid sending it to a colleague as a nickname; “bunny” is intimate and can feel overfamiliar.
Be careful using it about a woman you do not know well, because some readers will hear the Playboy connotation.
Do not assume a 🐰 in a fan comment is about animals; check whether it refers to an artist first.
design: Vendors draw a rabbit’s head from the front with two long ears standing straight up, a pink nose and visible buck teeth. Apple’s is light gray-white with pink inner ears; Google’s and Samsung’s are similar, with small shifts in fur tone and eye style. The expression is neutral and friendly everywhere. Because the designs agree, the emoji reads the same on every phone.

faqs.q: What does 🐰 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: Generally that she is feeling cute or playful, or that she thinks you are. Many people simply like rabbits or use bunny imagery as part of a soft personal style. It is also a favorite among BTS fans, so it may point to fandom rather than flirting.

faqs.q: Does the bunny emoji mean something sexual?
faqs.a: It can allude to the Playboy bunny or to the saying about rabbits and frequent sex, and some people use it that way on dating apps. Those uses are occasional. Around Easter or beside pet photos, there is no hidden meaning.

Members of BTS are each associated with an animal emoji by fans, and the rabbit belongs to Jungkook because of his smile and front teeth. Fans add 🐰 to posts and comments to refer to him without typing his name.

faqs.q: How can I tell 🐰 and 🐇 apart?
faqs.a: One is a face and one is the whole animal. 🐰 is the expressive, cute option for holidays and nicknames. 🐇 fits literal rabbits, running fast and Alice in Wonderland references such as following the white rabbit.
